extracted.intended_audience: students and general readers of philosophy, theology, and the science–religion interface
extracted.subtask_description: Philosophical method for locating and defending the abstract common ground between religious and scientific thought; includes methodological warnings about symbolic conceptions and the conceivability of cosmological hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual recognition of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Each side has to recognize the claims of the other as standing for truths that are not to be ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The religious point of view should regard Science as one constituent of the great whole and treat it with a sentiment like that which the remainder excites; conversely Science should treat Religion as a constituent of the great whole and as a subject of scientific inquiry with no more prejudice than any other reality. Both parties must strive to understand the other, convinced the other has something worthy to be understood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek a fundamental common verity
rubrics_metrics.description: Find that ultimate, most abstract truth which both Religion and Science will avow with absolute sincerity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The common ground must be an element so abstract that it underlies diverse religious forms and is more general than any particular scientific doctrine — a truth 'from which the several branches of Science diverge, from their common root.' The aim is not an ad hoc compromise but a real, permanent reconciliation founded on a substantive shared verity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid makeshift compromises
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not reconcile them in any makeshift way or by artificial, temporary compromises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reconciliation sought must be one that neither side need yield to — 'There shall be no concession — no yielding on either side' — but a meeting on common ground each will maintain; avoid solutions whose proposers secretly feel are artificial and temporary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate opposed convictions to produce higher synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Coalesce antagonist ideas, each containing a portion of truth, to produce a higher development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author uses analogies from geology, biology, psychology, and sociology to show how fusing competing hypotheses (igneous and aqueous; types and adaptations; innate and experiential theories) yields progress. Similarly, combining conclusions of Religion and Science should yield important results and modify our general theory of things.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground must be more abstract than particular doctrines
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither specific religious dogmas nor special scientific doctrines can serve as the basis of agreement; the shared truth must be more general than any particular science or creed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: trinitarian/unitarian dogmas or doctrines of propitiation cannot be accepted by Science; generalizations about space, time, matter, or force belonging to a particular science cannot become Religious conceptions. The common datum must underlie all branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy condition for symbolic conceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Symbolic conceptions are legitimate only if they can be verified by cumulative/indirect processes or by the fulfilment of predictions; otherwise they are vicious and illusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large magnitudes, durations, and extensive classes are often thought of symbolically. Such symbolic conceptions 'are indispensable' provided we can, by some cumulative or indirect thought-process or predictive success, assure ourselves they correspond to actualities; if no such verification is possible, they are 'altogether vicious and illusive' and indistinguishable from pure fictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware mistaking symbols for real conceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not habitually mistake symbolic (inadequate) conceptions for complete, real conceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As groups grow larger and more heterogeneous, the typical samples in thought become less like the average objects contained. There is an insensible transition from adequate to symbolic conceptions; because symbols often serve practical purposes, we are prone to accept them without verification and so open the door to error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceivability as a criterion for acceptable hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypotheses that are literally unthinkable (not merely improbable) must be rejected; conceivability is decisive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three common suppositions about the origin of the universe — self-existence, self-creation (pantheism), and creation by external agency (theism) — are argued to be 'literally unthinkable' because they involve the impossible idea of self-existence or require infinite regress. The test applied is whether the elements of a hypothesis can be put together in consciousness or rendered into actual thoughts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogy must address the central mystery
rubrics_metrics.description: Analogies (e.g., the artisan-manufacturer analogy) are invalid if they do not help explain the essential problem (the origin of matter and space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The artisan simile may vaguely symbolize a method of arrangement but fails to explain 'whence the pre-existing elements' or the production of matter out of nothing. An analogy is worthless if it sidesteps the real explanatory challenge (including the conceivability of space's origin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek the largest/ultimate fact within mental range
rubrics_metrics.description: The common truth sought must be the largest fact we can find within our mental range — the ultimate fact uniting the positive and negative poles of human thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniting religion and science requires identifying 'the largest fact' underlying both. This ultimate fact should be such that recognizing it profoundly modifies our conception of the Universe, life, human nature, and moral ideas.
